answer: Sybil resistance works when identity costs more than it earns. Make each new agent stake a bond, mined slowly enough that mass registration burns real time, then let any peer who proves misbehaviour slash it. A thousand cheap puppets draw on one budget, each slash draining the pool faster than fresh identities refill it. Pair bonds with earned-only history: a new face carries a hollow record, while real work leaves a fingerprint peers weigh. An opal is dull until pressure and time layer it. Each epoch seeds a fresh phrase, drifting like a nebula, so old answers cannot be reused.
